name: Jellyfin Federation
description: Aggregate content from multiple Jellyfin servers into unified virtual libraries
overview: The Jellyfin Federation Plugin allows you to create a unified media library by aggregating content from multiple remote Jellyfin servers. Stream content from any server without file synchronization.
changelog: Builds on 0.0.31's dedup/badge/resume work with the new adaptive WAN bitrate cap for Direct mode, plus two real bugs found while testing it - still no forced item recreation (existing watch progress and ids are untouched): (1) item.Path was stamped once, at the moment an item was first created, with whatever WanBandwidthMonitor happened to decide at that instant - but reconciliation never revisits an existing item, so that decision froze forever even after later classification or a fresh bandwidth measurement changed what the correct answer should now be. Depending purely on when each item happened to be created, some played the raw file and some played a capped transcode regardless of what the connection currently needed - reported directly as 'it doesn't work for every single file'. A static Path is now only ever stamped when it provably cannot go stale (WanCapMode Off, or Auto once a server is positively confirmed same-network) - everything else always resolves fresh on every playback request instead. (2) The live per-request path had a matching bug: it reported the original source's real container/codecs even when actually serving a capped transcode, which could confuse direct-play negotiation. (3) Also: removing a remote server now immediately cleans up after itself - its federated items are reconciled out of the library right away instead of lingering until the next sync, and its cached WAN classification/bandwidth data is dropped instead of leaking in memory.
